literal: He, Lady Cao, and the five children accepted gifts at seven places; Jian indulged them all and refused nothing they asked.
idiomatic: He, Cao, and their five children took bribes at seven posts; Jian went along with everything they wanted.

literal: Thereafter cases were settled by bribe; takings lay in heaps; the people of Qi suffered bitterly, and Jian's reputation for good rule was gravely damaged.
idiomatic: Prison outcomes went to the highest bidder; bribes piled up; Qi groaned under it, and Jian's name for clean government was ruined.

literal: At the start of Shizong's reign he was transferred from his standing rank as general to Inspector of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: When Shizong came to the throne he left his standing generalship for the Xuzhou inspectorate.

literal: Xuzhou and Yanzhou suffered great floods; many people starved; Jian memorialized for added relief, and the people were thereby saved.
idiomatic: Flood struck Xu and Yan; famine spread; Jian asked for extra relief, and the province was kept alive.

literal: Earlier, Prince of Jingzhao Yu had held Xuzhou; the prince being young, Chief Administrator Lu Yuan governed those below with leniency, and commanderies and counties mostly did not obey the law.
idiomatic: Before this, Prince Yu of Jingzhao had governed Xuzhou; he was young, and Chief Administrator Lu Yuan ruled the staff loosely, so counties rarely kept the law.

literal: Jian memorialized: "Cheng Lingqiu, Administrator of Liang Commandery, is addicted only to wine, greedy in pursuit of wealth, cruel in government and ruinous to the people; bandits and robbers rise together; licentious sounds and perverse clamor fill the roads; within his jurisdiction people lament; all alike resent his cruelty.
idiomatic: Jian wrote: "Cheng Lingqiu, prefect of Liang, drinks without cease, hoards wealth, tortures his people, and lets bandits run wild; obscene songs and riotous noise choke the roads; his district wails; everyone calls him cruel."

literal: Liang Commandery borders closely on the false capital-region; ugly reports spread easily; not only would this blemish pure winds—I fear we will be mocked in distant wastes.
idiomatic: Liang lies hard against the Southern capital; scandal travels fast; it will stain more than local reputations—we may be laughed at in the borderlands.

literal: I request dismissal from the office he holds, to clarify penal statutes."
idiomatic: I ask that he be removed from office so the law may be seen to bite."

literal: An edict dismissed Lingqiu from the commandery and summoned him back to the capital; thereafter Xuzhou's territory became orderly.
idiomatic: The throne stripped Lingqiu of Liang and recalled him to the capital; Xu grew quiet after that.

literal: His eldest son Bozong, Outer Office Gentleman;
idiomatic: His eldest son Bozong was an outer-office gentleman;

literal: second Zhongyuan, Administrator of Lanling.
idiomatic: the second, Zhongyuan, was prefect of Lanling.

literal: Both died young.
idiomatic: Both died young.

literal: Zhongyuan's younger brother Jiwei, in the Wuding era, was Central Army Aide of the Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: Zhongyuan's younger brother Jiwei, in the Wuding era, served as central army aide to the Grand Marshal.

literal: He, styled Shanyi.
idiomatic: He, styled Shanyi.

literal: After Jian's death, he contended with Jian's son Bozong to succeed to the fief.
idiomatic: After Jian died, he fought Jian's son Bozong over the succession.

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Gao memorialized: "In the Taihe era He left office to become a monk and yielded the title to Jian.
idiomatic: Director Gao Zhao wrote: "In Taihe, He took the tonsure and gave the fief to Jian.

literal: Later Jian, because He's son Xian was still in his weak-crown years and ought to inherit the foundation, asked to yield the princely title and return it to the rightful heir.
idiomatic: Later Jian, seeing He's son Xian still barely grown, asked to step aside and restore the line to the true heir.

literal: The former court's edict held for Jian's lifetime and granted his request.
idiomatic: The prior reign allowed this for Jian's lifetime.

literal: After Jian had died, He sought to inherit the enfeoffment.
idiomatic: When Jian was gone, He pressed to inherit the title.

literal: Carefully tracing the edict's intent, it allowed transmission to son Xian and did not permit it to his person.
idiomatic: The edict, read closely, passed the fief to Xian, not to He himself.

literal: He first yielded and afterward sought—contrary to constant principle; I request that Bozong inherit the fief."
idiomatic: He yielded, then demanded—against all decency; let Bozong succeed."

literal: Shizong's edict said: "He at first yielded to Jian, and Jian in turn yielded to his son; the way of mutual yielding is thereby made manifest.
idiomatic: Shizong ruled: "He first yielded to Jian, and Jian yielded back to He's son; their exchange of deference stands as an example.

literal: His son died young; He may be permitted to inherit."
idiomatic: That son died young; let He inherit."

literal: Shortly he was appointed Remonstrating Grandee and concurrent Master of the Crown Prince's Rate Revision; then transferred to Direct-palace Scattered Cavalier Attendant and concurrent Eastern Central Army General.
idiomatic: He was soon made remonstrating grandee and concurrent master of the crown prince's rate revision, then direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant and eastern central army general.

literal: In Suzong's time he went out as Supporting-the-State General and Inspector of Liangzhou and was dismissed for an offense.
idiomatic: Under Suzong he went out as supporting-the-state general and Liangzhou inspector, then was dismissed for a crime.

literal: After a long while he was appointed Administrator of Dongjun.
idiomatic: Long afterward he was made prefect of Dongjun.

literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguang he died; posthumously made Pacifying-the-East General and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: He died in Zhenguang 4 and was posthumously made pacifying-the-east general and Xiangzhou inspector.

literal: His son Qian, styled Siyi, inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Qian, styled Siyi, inherited the fief.

literal: Later appointed Forward Army General and Commander-in-Chief for Subduing the Barbarians.
idiomatic: Later he was made forward army general and commander for subduing the barbarians.

literal: At the start of Zhuangdi's reign he met disaster at Heyin.
idiomatic: At the start of Zhuangdi's reign he was killed at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously made Scattered Cavalier Attendant, General Who Subdues the East, Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was scattered cavalier attendant, general who subdues the east, bearer of ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and Xiangzhou inspector.

literal: His son Sen inherited.
idiomatic: His son Sen inherited.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, noble ranks were reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, noble ranks were lowered by precedent.

literal: Jian's younger brother Rong, styled Pisheng.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Rong, styled Pisheng.

literal: In Gaozu's time he was in the inner guard and followed the imperial carriage on the campaign against Xinye.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he served in the inner guard and followed the throne against Xinye.

literal: He ended as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: He ended as supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

literal: Rong's younger brother Liang, styled Bixie.
idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Liang, styled Bixie.

literal: General of Majestic Might and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: General of majestic might and supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

literal: He died; posthumously made Administrator of Hejian.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made prefect of Hejian.

literal: Liang's younger brother Kui, styled Daoming.
idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Kui, styled Daoming.

literal: Staff officer of the Grand Marshal's office, secretariat aide, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
idiomatic: He was staff officer in the Grand Marshal's office, secretariat aide, general who pacifies the distance, and vice director of the Imperial Stud.

literal: He went out and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Eastern Qinzhou.
idiomatic: He left court as general who pacifies the west and inspector of Eastern Qin.

literal: At the start of Jianyi he died in the province; [4] posthumously made General Who Subdues the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: In the opening of Jianyi he died in office; [4] posthumously he was general who subdues the east and Qingzhou inspector.

literal: Prince of Hejian Xiu was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: Prince Xiu of Hejian was enfeoffed in Tiansi 4.

literal: In the first year of Taichang he died, without sons.
idiomatic: In Taichang 1 he died without heirs.

literal: Shizu continued the extinguished line and ordered Jie'er, son of Prince of Henan Yao, to inherit Xiu's title, changing the enfeoffment to Lüeyang.
idiomatic: Shizu revived the line and had Jie'er, son of Prince Yao of Henan, succeed Xiu, re-enfeoffed as Prince of Lüeyang.

literal: Later, with King of Yongchang Jian he directed the armies in punishing Tufa Baozhou at Fanhe, moved several hundred households of Zhangye people to Wuwei, and then with the generals privately seized them for themselves.
idiomatic: Later he and King Jian of Yongchang marched on Tufa Baozhou at Fanhe, moved hundreds of Zhangye households to Wuwei, then with other commanders kept them for private spoil.

literal: For greed and violence his rank was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: For greed and violence his rank was cut to duke.

literal: Later he commanded the armies of Hexi in a raid on the Rouran, reaching the desert south.
idiomatic: Later he led the Hexi armies against the Rouran as far as the southern desert.

literal: His princely title was restored and he was made additional General Who Subdues the West.
idiomatic: His princely title was restored and he was made additional general who subdues the west.

literal: At the start of Zhengping, for a crime he was granted death; the title was extinguished.
idiomatic: At the start of Zhengping he was sentenced to death for a crime; the fief was abolished.

literal: Prince of Changle Chuwen was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: Prince Chuwen of Changle was enfeoffed in Tiansi 4.

literal: From childhood he was clever and eloquent.
idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and quick-tongued.

literal: At fourteen, in the first year of Taichang he died; Taizong mourned him, from the small encoffment to the burial always coming in person to grieve.
idiomatic: He died at fourteen in Taichang 1; Taizong mourned him, attending every rite from encoffment to burial.

literal: He was buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Without sons, the title was extinguished.
idiomatic: He left no son; the fief lapsed.

literal: Prince of Guangping Lian was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi.
idiomatic: Prince Lian of Guangping was enfeoffed in Tiansi 4.

literal: In the fourth year of Shiguang he died, without sons.
idiomatic: In Shiguang 4 he died without heirs.

literal: Shizu continued the extinguished line and made Hun, second son of Prince of Yangping Xi, Prince of Nanping to continue Lian's line, with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the West.
idiomatic: Shizu revived the line by making Hun, second son of Prince Xi of Yangping, Prince of Nanping to continue Lian, with additional general who pacifies the west.

literal: Hun loved bow and horse; shooting birds, he would kill them in flight one after another; [5] at the time all marveled.
idiomatic: Hun loved archery and horses; shooting birds, he would kill them on the wing in succession; [5] everyone marveled.

literal: Shizu once ordered those at his side to shoot in competition; whoever hit the target filled the tally; he ordered Hun to release, and all three shots hit; Shizu was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: Shizu once had his attendants shoot for stakes; whoever hit filled the tally; Hun was told to shoot and hit three times running; Shizu was delighted.

literal: He prized Hun's skill and constantly kept him at his side, granting a hundred horses and several tens of servants.
idiomatic: He prized Hun's skill, kept him close, and gave him a hundred horses and several dozen servants.

literal: Later appointed with provisional credentials, Commander-in-Chief of Pingzhou Armies, Colonel Protecting the Eastern Yi, General Who Guards the East, Bearer of Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Pingzhou, garrisoning Helong.
idiomatic: Later he held provisional credentials, commanded Pingzhou armies, protected the eastern Yi as colonel, guarded the east as general, bore ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and governed Pingzhou from Helong.

literal: In the province his pacification and guidance were effective; Chinese and foreigners alike were pleased.
idiomatic: In office his rule was sound; settlers and tribes alike were content.

literal: He was moved to Garrison Commander of Liangzhou, Commander of Western Rong Armies, and Colonel Protecting the Western Regions, and granted two imperial horses.
idiomatic: He was shifted to Liangzhou garrison commander, commander of western Rong armies, and colonel protecting the western regions, with two imperial horses.

literal: On taking the post he was pure and cautious; his kindness was felt throughout Liang.
idiomatic: He took office chaste and careful; his kindness spread through Liang.

literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, elders wept and followed to send him off as if parting from kin.
idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to court, elders wept and followed him as if losing kin.

literal: In the eleventh year of Taihe, while following the imperial carriage on a tour of Mount Fangshan, he died on the road.
idiomatic: In Taihe 11, following the throne on a tour of Mount Fangshan, he died on the road.

literal: His son Feilong inherited; later he was granted the name Xiao.
idiomatic: His son Feilong inherited; later he was granted the name Xiao.

literal: Nine feet in height, a belt ten spans around, his bearing towering.
idiomatic: He stood nine feet tall, belt ten spans round, towering in bearing.

literal: He had elegant bearing and was pure and upright in an outstanding way; he loved to speak blunt remonstrance, and court ministers feared him.
idiomatic: He had style, stood unbending, loved blunt counsel, and ministers feared him.

literal: Gaozu especially favored him, appointing him Director of the Imperial Clan and Right Honored Grandee; an edict said: "From now on in memorials, all ministers may be addressed by personal name; only the Prince of Nanping may be addressed directly by his title.
idiomatic: Gaozu favored him especially, made him director of the imperial clan and right honored grandee, and ruled: "In memorials hereafter all ministers may be named; only the Prince of Nanping may be named by his title."

literal: He was moved to Left Honored Grandee.
idiomatic: He was moved to left honored grandee.

literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he died; granted one set of court robes, one suit of garments, first-grade Eastern Garden secret coffin ware, and a thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: In Taihe 17 he died; the court gave court robes, a suit, first-grade eastern garden coffin ware, and a thousand bolts of silk.

literal: Gaozu wore hemp mourning and came in person to Xiao's funeral, grieving so that those around him were moved; feasts did not raise music.
idiomatic: Gaozu came in hemp mourning to Xiao's rites, grieving those around him; banquets went without music.

literal: Posthumously made Guards General and Inspector of Dingzhou, with five hundred bolts of silk granted.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was guards general and Dingzhou inspector, with five hundred bolts of silk.

literal: Posthumous title: Prince An.
idiomatic: His posthumous title was Prince An.

literal: His son Zuan inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited.

literal: Zuan also had reputation in his time; appointed Restoring Martial General, advanced to General Who Pacifies the West, and concurrent Western Central Army General; he went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Pingzhou.
idiomatic: Zuan too was praised in his day; he was restoring martial general, then general who pacifies the west and western central army general, then general who pacifies the north and Pingzhou inspector.

literal: In the first year of Jingming he died at Pingcheng.
idiomatic: In Jingming 1 he died at Pingcheng.

literal: His son Bohe inherited.
idiomatic: His son Bohe inherited.

literal: In the third year of Yongping he died; posthumously made Scattered Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; posthumous title Prince Ai.
idiomatic: In Yongping 3 he died; posthumously scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; posthumous title Prince Ai.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Tong died; posthumously made Inspector of Liangzhou.
idiomatic: Tong died; posthumously he was Liangzhou inspector.

literal: His son Silue, at the end of Wuding, was Administrator of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: His son Silue, late in Wuding, was Yingzhou administrator.

literal: Silue's younger brother Shulue, in Wuding, was chief clerk of the Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: Silue's younger brother Shulue, in Wuding, was chief clerk of the Grand Marshal.

literal: Prince of Jingzhao Li was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Tiansi and died in the first year of Shenjue.
idiomatic: Prince Li of Jingzhao was enfeoffed in Tiansi 4 and died in Shenjue 1.

literal: His son Gen inherited, changed enfeoffment to Prince of Jiangyang, with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: His son Gen inherited, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangyang, and made additional general who pacifies the north.

literal: He died without sons; Xianzu made Xiao, second son of Prince of Nanping Xiao, continue Gen's line.
idiomatic: He died without heirs; Xianzu made Xiao, second son of Prince Xiao of Nanping, continue Gen's line.

literal: Ji, styled Shiren.
idiomatic: Ji, styled Shiren.

literal: He inherited as Prince of Jiangyang with additional rank as General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: He inherited as Prince of Jiangyang with additional general who pacifies the north.

literal: In Gaozu's time he was appointed Bearer of Credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, and Commander-in-Chief of Fuming Garrison; transferred to Commander of Rouxuan, Fuming, and Huaihuang Garrisons Armies, General Who Guards the North, and Commander of Rouxuan Garrison.
idiomatic: Under Gaozu he bore credentials as general who pacifies the north and Fuming garrison commander, then commanded Rouxuan, Fuming, and Huaihuang garrisons as general who guards the north.

literal: He entered court as Left Guards General, concurrent Palace Attendant, then also concurrent Central Army Commander, remaining to guard Luoyang.
idiomatic: He entered as left guards general and palace attendant, then also central army commander, guarding Luoyang.

literal: Shortly he was appointed Bearer of Credentials and General Who Pacifies the North, garrisoning and overseeing the old capital.
idiomatic: Soon he bore credentials as general who pacifies the north, garrisoning the old capital.

literal: The Gaoche chieftain Shuze gathered his tribes in rebellion; an edict made Ji commander-in-chief of the northern punitive armies; from Huaishuo east all obeyed Ji's command.
idiomatic: Gaoche chief Shuze rebelled with his tribes; Ji was made commander of northern punitive armies; from Huaishuo east all fell under his command.

literal: Ji memorialized: "The Gaoche are a stubborn faction that do not know awe and statute; lightly they gather together, desert service, and flee back.
idiomatic: Ji wrote: "The Gaoche are stubborn and know neither awe nor law; they band lightly, desert duty, and flee.

literal: Considering their fierce cruelty, by right they should be driven to extremity; if all are pursued and slaughtered, I fear disorder will follow.
idiomatic: By rights they should be destroyed root and branch; but wholesale slaughter may only spread chaos.

literal: I request that envoys be sent to each garrison to investigate and execute only the chief culprit; for the rest, add comfort and instruction—if they repent and return to service, let them join the army."
idiomatic: Send envoys to each post to investigate, behead one ringleader, comfort the rest, and let any who repent return to the ranks."

literal: An edict followed this.
idiomatic: The throne agreed.
